acceptance.reason: An independent mock CLI-runtime probe requested and approved a workspace write and a shell command. approved.txt and shell.txt were created, two approval.decided events recorded policy=balanced, and artifact.recorded plus session.completed were persisted. pnpm test passed 33/33 including the tool-loop coverage.

apps/cli/src/render.ts renders approvals, resumed approvals, diffs, command stdout/stderr and exit codes, usage, and completion. The Linux, Darwin, and Windows TUI smoke reports each contain 12/12 exit-zero results with timeline, approval, diff, usage, and completion true; each smoke hash matches its persona report.

The provider configuration path carries base URL, credential reference, model, and protocol through all three adapters. All three protocol-smoke records completed a real streaming session with vendor-prefixed model commandcode-plan/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash and canonical model deepseek-flash. The official DeepSeek URL uses the same openai-chat path, although the official endpoint itself was not directly invoked in this environment.

The pre-dispatch guard rejects a non-DeepSeek request model, but the returned provider model is not checked. An independent probe requested deepseek-flash from all three adapters while the provider returned model gpt-4.1; every adapter accepted and normalized the response (chat, Responses, and Anthropic text) instead of rejecting it. This violates the spec scenario where a provider returns a non-DeepSeek model.

The agent appends assistant reasoningContent and tool calls before the tool result, and the passing tool-loop test observes the prior reasoning_content in the second request. The request path always carries the selected reasoning effort, and live persona events show multi-turn tool loops completing without reasoning-continuity errors.

buildStableSystemPrefix is deterministic across reversed tool ordering and omits volatile nonce data in optimized mode. model.completed events persist input, output, cache-hit, cache-miss, reasoning, latency, and provider model data; persona and A/B evidence contain populated cache telemetry.

Resolution covers auto, canonical, compatibility aliases, and unambiguous vendor-prefixed DeepSeek names. session.created, model.selected, and model.requested persist the provider model, canonical model, and selection reason. An independent CLI probe with deepseek-v4-pro recorded 'alias deepseek-v4-pro -> deepseek-flash'; the active registry has only one canonical model, so the conditional alternative-override branch is not instantiated.

An independent workspace-auto probe automatically approved and recorded a workspace write while separately gating command and network actions. The command and web_fetch were denied before execution, while the write succeeded. Events recorded policy=workspace-auto, automatic=true for the write, explicit non-automatic denials for the other actions, and the session completed.

The targeted resume test passed: the original event history and pending approval were preserved, approval.resumed was emitted, the dangling write executed, artifact.recorded was persisted, and the tool result reached the next model request before completion.

The passing redaction test covers bearer, API-key, authorization, and token forms; tool command environments are sanitized of credential-like variables; provider and tool errors call redact. A repository-wide scan of dist JSON evidence found no raw sk-, bearer, authorization, or api-key values.

An independent headless CLI probe parsed every stdout line as JSON. A blocked write exited 3 with last record type approval-required plus sessionId and resume command; workspace-auto exited 0 with a final result record and completed session. The CLI also defines stable exit categories 0 through 5.

The passing test suite rejects invalid/non-HTTPS or credential-bearing URLs, missing credentials, unsupported protocols, non-DeepSeek request identifiers, and unsupported capabilities before adapter dispatch. Probes observe zero provider requests and no session creation for locally knowable failures; a non-empty invalid credential can only be authenticated by the provider.

pnpm release:check reports Linux 22,012 bytes, Darwin 22,063 bytes, and Windows 22,086 bytes, all below 50,000,000. Each tar archive contains only package.json and the 96,924-byte neonforge.mjs bundle, with no model weights, browser engine, or bundled Node runtime. All three extracted bundles ran 'node neonforge.mjs version' successfully.

The Linux, Darwin, and Windows TUI smoke reports are bound to source revision 64b5bff4c9155abc7d6fad0d1234f9b0910b2a08f01f5ade019bdcb9b9d447ff. Each has 12 exit-zero completed scenarios with timeline, approval, diff, usage, and completion true, and each report hash link verifies against its persona report.

pnpm test passed all protocol streaming, tool-call, reasoning, usage, provider-error, cancellation, and outbound DeepSeek-policy tests for all three adapters. An independent Responses probe observed input items [user, assistant, function_call, function_call_output] with call_id call-1 and no role=tool, tool_calls, or tool_call_id fields; all three real streaming smoke records passed.

Each platform report contains 12 unique personas and 12/12 passed scenarios, for 36/36 total. Every deterministic assertion is true, all 12 evaluators per platform returned pass, and all reports have zero P0 and zero P1 defects. The simulator and evaluator are separate model sessions.

benchmarks/external-baseline.json records three DeepSeek-published sources with URLs, publisher, model and benchmark versions, retrieval date, raw values, units, and aggregation methods. SHA-256 over JSON.stringify(sources) recomputes to 975bd3fdcd9a65181d95d01d55d58d6cbb0c0c0cc20f5fe60ef5975effb884e8, matching the recorded integrity hash; all local source hashes also match the registry.

Formal A18 is the efficiency item. Independent recomputation from the six paired samples gives cost per successful task of $0.001919082 versus $0.004104233 (53.241% lower), median wall time of 13,176.5 ms versus 15,644 ms (15.773% lower), and optimized success 6/6 versus baseline 5/6 (negative regression). The 15% cost, 10% time, and 2-point no-regression criteria are met.

Formal A19 is the local baseline registry. pnpm baseline:verify passed offline with 2 confirmed entries and 3 staged candidates, and pnpm baseline:adapter validated 105 bugs, 2 repositories, 5 attempts, 10,800 seconds per repository, and V2 target 40.4. All 20 local source hashes and both normalized hashes recompute correctly; Bug Hunt is status=confirmed, canonical=false with scoreClaim=null, and V1 makes no Bug Hunt score claim.

risks: A4 is a product defect: a provider-returned non-DeepSeek model is accepted by all three adapters after a DeepSeek request.

Real provider smoke used a loopback Magpie-compatible DeepSeek gateway rather than directly invoking api.deepseek.com; the official endpoint configuration path was inspected but not exercised end-to-end.

The A/B time reduction is 15.773%, but its six-sample bootstrap CI includes zero; only the median threshold and no-success-regression criteria are met. Optimized p95 wall time is also higher than baseline p95 in the guardrail data.
A non-empty invalid credential cannot be proven invalid without a provider response; only missing or locally invalid credentials are rejected before dispatch.
License/redistribution rationale for registry sources is documentary in benchmarks/sources/README.md and source headers rather than a structured field on each registry entry.
Native macOS and Windows TUI reports were inspected and hash-verified, while direct installer extraction and launch were rerun only on the current Linux host.

dist/, release evidence, CodeGraph, dependencies, and agent harness directories are intentionally untracked. The Git baseline contains only tracked product source, specs, tests, scripts, docs, benchmark sources, and .comet/config.yaml; no tracked home paths or credentials were found.
summary: Independent read-only verification passed all five required gates and confirmed clean Git-baseline provenance, but one formal acceptance item fails. A4 is not met because all three adapters accept a provider response model of gpt-4.1 when deepseek-flash was requested. A1-A3 and A5-A19 are supported by source inspection, passing tests, machine-readable evidence, independent behavioral probes, hash recomputation, and installer inspection. Final result: 18 passed, 1 failed, 0 blocked.
